title: AI doctors vs FutureClinic: how much a real doctor checks - FutureClinic
summary: AI doctor safety, and whether AI can replace doctors: Utah prescription filings, Lotus and FutureClinic compared, where a doctor reads every case.
body_markdown:
State filings, a company study, and founder interviews as of October 2026 show that human physician oversight on AI doctor apps for a rash, refill, or lingering symptom ranges from two-minute clinician sign-offs to planned 5% to 10% retrospective spot-checks.


On FutureClinic, a specific doctor reads your whole case and answers with a Human Signature: a live video or voice note recorded for you. No form is approved in bulk. You can message the same doctor over time in the same chat and get help with other problems in their specialty, like a dermatologist treating both acne and eczema, while every FutureClinic doctor you see works from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) .


We believe AI is a tool for doctors, with the doctor in charge of every case. Most health problems have nuance and need one-to-one attention, and only an expert can tell when an AI has made a mistake or is heading to the wrong answer. FutureClinic's AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident to gather your history and organize your case, never giving medical advice by itself.


## What do Utah's AI prescription filings say?


In[Utah's regulatory sandbox](https://commerce.utah.gov/ai/regulatory-relief-4/authorized-pilots/) as of October 2026,[Doctronic's agreement](https://commerce.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Doctronic-Final-Agreement.pdf) for routine non-controlled refills requires practitioner authorization for every Phase 1 request, then moves to a "Monthly review of 5-10% of all processed renewals" ([terms](https://www.doctronic.ai/terms-of-service/) allow refills "whether or not that physician reviews an individual renewal"). Co-CEO Dr. Adam Oskowitz told[Health Tech Nerds](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WYqQlzG8h2w&t=605s) (January 7, 2026, 10:05, YouTube's automatic captions) that next-phase doctors will independently review AI renewal decisions for 10% of patients, and CMO Dr. Byron Crowe told[Offcall](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yU8RV5FFeQQ&t=1083s) (March 12, 2026, 18:03, YouTube's automatic captions) the final stage shifts over time to full autonomy with after-the-fact review.


[August's Utah refill pilot](https://www.meetaugust.ai/press/utah-prescription-renewal-pilot) ($4 per refill as of October 2026; approved October 2, 2026, not started) reviews the first 250 refills beforehand; at its end state, "physicians spot-check 5% of decisions".[Nolla Health's Utah acne pilot](https://www.nollahealth.com/ai-prescriptions) (active October 5, 2026; $4.99/month, normally $9.99 as of October 2026) has two physicians approve each prescription for the first 100 patients, lets AI prescribe directly up to 500 patients, and then has physicians "review a sample of at least 10% of prescriptions every month". CEO Luis Wenus said in a[Fox News interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pMQKEIZHd4w&t=161s) Nolla posted on YouTube (October 12, 2026, 2:41, YouTube's automatic captions) that after 100 cases, the AI prescribes autonomously while doctors review retroactively.


## How many patients does one doctor oversee?


Outside Utah's pilots, Lotus and Nolla say a clinician approves every prescription. Lotus Health AI's[download page](https://lotus.ai/download) states "Lotus uses medical AI to make doctors 10x more productive". On[Lotus's YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zcNBXIrakxY&t=22s) (February 12, 2026, 0:22, YouTube's automatic captions), founder and CEO KJ Dhaliwal stated as a current fact that with a 10x gain, one doctor has a 20,000-patient panel. On[Boundless Life](https://bengreenfieldlife.com/lotus) (July 16, 2026, 18:27, 20:41), he said "the physician is there to review what the AI is coming up with and sign off on it," which "on the doctor's side, happens within about two minutes." On[Iron Foundry](https://tryterra.co/podcast/The-CEO-behind-the-AI-Doctor-41m-raised) (October 14, 2026, 42:07), asked if doctors are needed only for legal approval, Dhaliwal said, "mostly from a patient safety perspective and a regulatory perspective, yes, that's why the physician is there," adding it brings trust and humanity. In[Lotus's study](https://lotus.ai/news/evaluating-clinician-agreement-with-ai-proposed-care-actions-in-asynchronous-primary-care) (1,678 AI actions, 244 patients), "clinicians approved 98% of proposals that reached a final non-pending verdict", and "Prescriptions had the highest rejection rate at 10.2%".


Counsel Health CEO Dr. Muthu Alagappan told[Fitt Insider](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GiMxaBBA5Wg&t=445s) (January 26, 2026, 7:09 to 7:48, YouTube's automatic captions) that Counsel doctors currently see 15 to 20-plus patients hourly using software where they approve or deny a plan in one click, targeting single-click visits. On[Offcall](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7l2pvqrRhFU&t=1937s) (September 3, 2026, 32:17, YouTube's automatic captions), Counsel CMO Dr. Rishi Khakhkhar described a 2036 target of 100,000-person panels, and a16z partner Julie Yoo (a Counsel investor) wrote on[Substack](https://healthtechbuilders.substack.com/p/ai-as-a-new-site-of-care) (September 18, 2025), naming no company, that AI-native care is "enabling effective panel sizes of 10,000+ patients per doctor." In a[March 25, 2026 post](https://www.doctronic.ai/blog/the-status-quo-is-the-biggest-risk/) , Doctronic co-CEOs Matt Pavelle and Dr. Adam Oskowitz wrote their clinic runs "6-7x more efficiently than a traditional practice, and we expect to hit 10x by year-end," adding that requiring "'only with a physician reviewing every single case,' then we've decided the physician shortage is permanent and acceptable. We don't accept that."
